issues.detail: The Greek word 'λοιμον' (loimon) means 'plague' or 'pestilence'. The Vietnamese translation 'bệnh dịch' is a literal translation of 'plague', but the grammatical structure in Vietnamese ('là một bệnh dịch') treats it as a noun phrase identifying the man as a plague, whereas the Greek 'ευροντες... τον ανδρα τουτον λοιμον' functions as an accusative of quality or a descriptive construction. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'là' (is) is an addition that turns a descriptive attribute into a predicate identity.
The Greek 'πρωτοστατην τε της των ναζωραιων αιρεσεως' uses the word 'τε' (also/and), which is omitted in the Vietnamese translation, slightly altering the flow of the list of attributes.
